```python
from typing import List
from collections import Counter


def remove_duplicates(numbers: List[int]) -> List[int]:
    """ From a list of integers, remove all elements that occur more than once.
    Keep order of the remaining elements the same as in the input.
    """
    counts = Counter(numbers)
    return [n for n in numbers if counts[n] == 1]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert remove_duplicates([]) == []
    assert remove_duplicates([1, 2, 3, 4]) == [1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert remove_duplicates([1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 3, 5]) == [1, 4, 5]
    print("All tests passed.")
```

This follows the usual interpretation of this problem: any element that appears more than once is removed entirely, so `[1, 2, 3, 2, 4]` becomes `[1, 3, 4]`. It counts occurrences in one pass, then keeps only elements that occurred exactly once, preserving their original order, in O(n) time.
